entries.title: One row per session with what the reviewers said
entries.summary: In the Report Builder, add a scorecard question to a Sessions report and it arrives summarised for each session: Yes/No and other choices as counts (**Yes: 2 / No: 1**), scales and scores as an average, comments with the reviewer's initials. Speakers and tags can still be pivoted, so the report stays one row per session. **How to show this** switches a question to **One row per review**, and **Reviews pivot** gives one block of columns per reviewer. In SbQL: `COUNT_BY_VALUE` and `LIST_WITH_REVIEWER`, and review aggregates next to ordinary columns summarise each session.

where.path: Reporting → Reports → Report Builder → Fields → Reviews

entries.use_case: A conference committee wants one spreadsheet row per submission with the session details, the speakers, the average score, how many reviewers called it a sales pitch and every reviewer's final comment. CS built this for AVIXA with SQL; it is now a few clicks in the Report Builder.

cs_action.note: No setup. Reports that already exist are unchanged.

internal.gotchas: Abstentions are left out of the counts and comments. On a blind Review plan comments are listed without initials. The summaries count each review once even when a session has several speakers or tags.
internal.staff_path: Reporting → Reports → Report Builder (Sessions) → search a question → click it
internal.talk_track: Pick your scorecard questions by name and get one row per session, with the Yes/No counts and comments already summarised.
internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer asks for a review summary sheet, Yes/No tallies per submission, or comments from every reviewer next to the session details.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers running Plan 2.0 Review plans, especially CFP programs that hand a summary sheet to a program committee.

entries.title: Map Your Show: bring exhibitors and their booth contacts in for Advocacy
entries.summary: The **Map Your Show** app brings one show's active exhibitors into a Sessionboard event, with booths, website, description and logo, and links every booth contact with an email to their company. You can then run a Groups Advocacy campaign and **Email exhibitors** their own share links, with no portal and no spreadsheet. Syncs update only what changed in Map Your Show, keep your own edits, never create duplicates and never delete. Your Customer Success Manager connects it with the show's MYS API username, password and show code.

enable.path: Your Customer Success Manager connects the Map Your Show app for the show

where.path: Apps → Map Your Show (connected by Sessionboard)

entries.use_case: Trade show organizers whose exhibitor data lives in Map Your Show can pull every exhibitor and their contacts into Sessionboard automatically, then launch an Advocacy Groups campaign and email each contact a personal share link — without manually building the exhibitor list first.

cs_action.note: Staff-only until a real show has been connected and checked (first customer: IAAPA). Connect it with the customer's MYS API username, password and show code, then follow the first-live-run checklist in sessionboard-tam docs/integrations/mys-exhibitors.md.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a trade show or expo customer says their exhibitor list lives in Map Your Show and they want to run Advocacy for exhibitors or give exhibitors portal access without a manual import.
internal.who_should_get_it: Trade show and expo organizers — especially associations like IAAPA — who use Map Your Show as their exhibitor management system and want to run Advocacy Groups campaigns targeting exhibitor contacts.
internal.staff_path: Apps catalog → Map Your Show (staff-only gate must be lifted first)
internal.gotchas: The connector is marked staff-only in the catalog until a live show is verified — do not install it for customers yet. Response field names from the MYS API are assumed from third-party guides and not live-verified; the field mapping UI is editable if names differ. Logos are re-hosted into Sessionboard's CDN because MYS file links expire after 30 minutes. Contacts are never unlinked by a sync; categories, sponsors and contact unlinking are not in this release.
internal.talk_track: If your exhibitors are in Map Your Show, Sessionboard can pull them in automatically — accounts, contacts, booths and logos — so you can email every exhibitor contact a personal Advocacy link without building the list by hand.

draft.docs_gap: The App Marketplace guide should add a Map Your Show section covering: connecting the app, mapping an event, what syncs (exhibitor fields, booth assignments, logos, contacts), how the change-only write works, how to trigger a manual sync, and how to use the synced companies in an Advocacy Groups campaign.
draft.why_use_it: The App Marketplace lets you connect Sessionboard to the other platforms your event runs on, so data flows in automatically rather than through manual imports. Connecting Map Your Show keeps your exhibitor accounts and contacts current in Sessionboard, which unlocks Advocacy campaigns, portal access and CRM workflows for your exhibit hall without duplicate data entry. Field-level change tracking means a re-sync only writes what Map Your Show actually changed, so your team's edits in Sessionboard are never overwritten.

entries.title: Write engagement back to plain Salesforce, with optional Timeline Tasks
entries.summary: Orgs connected to Salesforce (without Fonteva or Nimble AMS) can now use **CRM Write-back** to push engagement, activity and suggestion data to Sessionboard's custom Salesforce objects. An optional **Timeline** toggle writes one completed standard Salesforce **Task** per activity row — subject lines such as "Spoke: Session Title — Event Name" or "Attended Event Name" — so engagement appears on the Contact's activity timeline in Salesforce. Write-back also runs on a daily schedule and pushes suggestion changes immediately after a suggestion is saved or decided.

where.path: CRM → Apps → Salesforce → Write-back

entries.use_case: An association using plain Salesforce (no Fonteva or Nimble AMS) can now push speaker, reviewer and attendee engagement back to Salesforce automatically each day, and optionally surface each activity as a completed Task on the Contact's timeline — giving membership and development teams a full picture of engagement without leaving Salesforce.

cs_action.note: Plain Salesforce customers (no Fonteva/Nimble) who have the CRM add-on are now eligible for write-back. Reach out to walk them through enabling it and, if they want activity timeline entries, turning on the Timeline toggle.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A Salesforce customer (without Fonteva or Nimble AMS) asks how to get engagement data back into Salesforce, or a current AMS write-back customer asks about Timeline Tasks.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any org on the CRM add-on with a plain Salesforce connection — associations, professional societies and event teams that use Salesforce as their system of record but do not run Fonteva or Nimble AMS.
internal.staff_path: CRM → Apps → Salesforce → Write-back; Timeline toggle is inside the write-back settings panel.
internal.gotchas: Timeline Tasks are opt-in and off by default; the toggle is only available for Salesforce connections (not HubSpot or Dataverse). Tasks are never deleted — a changed activity row is PATCHed, not removed. The daily write-back job runs at 07:00 by default (after the 06:30 people sync); nothing is written until at least one toggle is switched on. Nimble AMS WhatId on Person Accounts has not been confirmed in a live Nimble org.
internal.talk_track: If your team uses Salesforce, Sessionboard can now write every speaking engagement, attendance record, CE credit, review and award entry back to your Contacts automatically each day. You can also turn on Timeline Tasks so each activity shows up as a completed Task on the Contact record — no exports, no manual entry.

draft.docs_gap: The write-back guide should add a section covering plain Salesforce (non-AMS) setup, the Timeline toggle and its Task field mapping, the daily scheduled run, and the instant suggestion push behaviour.
draft.why_use_it: Write-back keeps your Salesforce Contacts up to date with every meaningful engagement recorded in Sessionboard — sessions spoken, events attended, CE credits earned, reviews completed and award entries submitted. Because the data lands on Sessionboard's own custom objects and, optionally, as standard Tasks on the Contact timeline, your membership, development and sales teams see the full engagement picture directly in Salesforce without running manual exports. Suggestions from the AI Speaker Finder reach Salesforce within seconds of being saved or decided, so your pipeline stays current throughout the planning cycle.
problems: src/data/release-notes/2026-11-12.json [crm-writeback-plain-salesforce-timeline-tasks] article /sessionboard-crm/ams/write-back is in a self-serve suite — set "product" to that suite, or link a Platform guide

entries.title: Pick an award program or course when using CRM Nominate and Enroll actions
entries.summary: The CRM **Nominate** and **Enroll** actions — available in the Salesforce package and HubSpot card — now include searchable pickers for award programs and courses. Instead of pasting a raw ID, users can search by name and select from a filtered list: only active award programs appear for **Nominate**, and only published courses appear for **Enroll**.

where.path: CRM → People → Nominate / Enroll action (Salesforce package or HubSpot card)

entries.use_case: A membership team using the Salesforce package can now search for and select the correct award program or learning course by name when nominating or enrolling a contact, eliminating the need to look up and paste internal IDs.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer using the Salesforce package or HubSpot card asks how to nominate contacts for awards or enroll them in courses without manually copying IDs.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers with the CRM add-on who use the Salesforce package or HubSpot card and run award programs or learning courses.
internal.staff_path: CRM → People → select a contact → Nominate or Enroll action in the Salesforce/HubSpot integration
internal.gotchas: The pickers are served by new API endpoints (/crm/org/:orgId/programs and /crm/org/:orgId/courses). The Public API routes and the Salesforce package picker UI ship in separate PRs (sessionboard-public-api and sessionboard-salesforce); this PR is the backend only.
internal.talk_track: Your team no longer needs to hunt down program or course IDs — they can search by name right inside Salesforce or HubSpot when nominating or enrolling a contact.

draft.docs_gap: The CRM overview guide should document the Nominate and Enroll actions, including how the award program and course pickers work and what filters apply (active programs only, published courses only).
draft.why_use_it: Sessionboard CRM connects your contacts to Awards and Learning so you can nominate or enroll people without leaving your existing tools. The Nominate and Enroll actions in the Salesforce package and HubSpot card let your team act on contacts in the systems they already use, keeping data in sync across your stack.

entries.title: Send Advocacy embed setup to your web team without requiring a Sessionboard login
entries.summary: On an Attendees campaign's **Share** tab, a new **Send setup** card lets you email the embed snippets and personal link template to up to 10 addresses (comma- or line-separated) with an optional note and a choice of registration platform. Each recipient gets a secure, login-free page at `/advocacy/setup/…` showing the **Personal card embed**, **Signup form embed**, **Open link** (when enabled), and **Personal link template**, each with a **Copy** button. The **Share** tab logs every send — address, sender, timestamp, platform, and **Opened / Not opened yet** status — and lets you **Turn off link** to revoke access at any time.

where.path: Marketing → Advocacy → [campaign] → Share → Send setup

entries.use_case: When a registration vendor or web agency needs to embed the Advocacy signup form or personal card on a confirmation page, an organizer can send them a secure, no-login setup page directly from the Share tab — no copy-pasting snippets into email, no Sessionboard account required for the recipient.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer says their registration vendor or web team can't access the Share tab, or when embed snippets are getting mangled by email link-rewriting.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer running an Attendees Advocacy campaign who relies on an outside vendor (registration platform, web agency) to place the embed code.
internal.staff_path: Marketing → Advocacy → [Attendees campaign] → Share → Send setup
internal.gotchas: The public setup page is token-based and login-free; tokens can be revoked from the Share tab log. The page is scrubbed from Sentry and Session Replay is disabled on it. Requires the companion API PR (same branch) to be deployed first.
internal.talk_track: You can now send your registration vendor a single link — no Sessionboard login needed — and see the moment they open it. If they leave the project, just turn off the link.

draft.docs_gap: The /marketing/advocacy-attendees guide should add a section explaining how to use Send setup to share embed snippets with an external web team, including how to read the send log and revoke a link.
draft.why_use_it: Advocacy for attendees lets you turn every registrant into a promoter by giving them a personal share card and signup embed they can put anywhere. Sending the embed code to an outside web team or registration vendor used to require a Sessionboard login or fragile copy-paste into email. The **Send setup** card delivers a clean, login-free page with every snippet and a copy button, so your vendor can drop the embeds into a confirmation page without touching the admin console. You can see when the link is opened and revoke it the moment the work is done.

entries.title: Timed quizzes, a question bank, in-video checkpoints and answer scoring in the course builder
entries.summary: The Learning course builder gains four new authoring capabilities. **Timed quizzes** let you set a time limit on any quiz block; a countdown timer runs for learners and per-learner extra time can be granted under **Learner** settings. The **Question bank** sheet (slash command **/ Questions from the bank** or **Save to question bank** under any question) lets you search, tag-filter, add, edit, archive and restore reusable questions across courses. **In-video checkpoints** are now edited directly under the video block. Under **Learning › Approvals › Answers to score**, reviewers can award points, add notes and see a live pass/fail preview for written-answer questions.

enable.path: Get started → Early Access → Preview → Learning

where.path: Learning → Courses → [course] → [lesson] → Quiz block / Question block; Learning → Approvals → Answers to score

entries.use_case: Course authors who need to simulate exam conditions can add a countdown timer to any quiz and grant extra time to individual learners. The question bank lets teams build a shared library of vetted questions that can be dropped into any course, and the Answers to score queue gives reviewers a structured place to grade open-ended responses with points and notes.

cs_action.note: All capabilities are inside the self-serve Learning workspace, gated behind the Learning preview. No Platform screen changes.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a Learning customer asks about timed assessments, question reuse across courses, or grading written answers.
internal.who_should_get_it: Learning workspace customers building certification or compliance courses that require timed exams or scored written responses.
internal.staff_path: Learning → Courses → [course] → lesson editor; Learning → Approvals → Answers to score
internal.gotchas: Timed quizzes and the question bank are self-serve Learning preview features; they do not appear in the Platform product. Extra time is granted per learner from the Learner panel, not from the quiz block itself.
internal.talk_track: You can now set a time limit on any quiz, save questions to a shared bank so every course author can reuse them, and grade open-ended answers with points and notes — all without leaving Sessionboard Learning.

draft.docs_gap: The existing questions-and-quizzes guide should add a section on timed quizzes and per-learner extra time; the question-bank guide should document the slash-command entry points and the archive/restore workflow; the score-written-answers guide should cover the new points, notes and live pass preview fields in the Approvals queue.
draft.why_use_it: The Sessionboard Learning course builder lets you write, arrange and publish interactive courses without leaving your event workspace. Quizzes, branching scenarios, video checkpoints and written-answer questions are all authored in one place, so your team can build rigorous, credit-bearing learning experiences alongside your program content. The question bank keeps your best questions reusable across courses, and the scoring queue gives reviewers a clear workflow for grading open-ended responses.

entries.title: Survey feedback import: a template, required columns, and a list of rows that won't import
entries.summary: The survey file import under **Record Settings > Participant portal > Feedback** now works like Sessionboard's other imports. **Download template** gives you a spreadsheet built for the event, with **Ratings**, **Comments**, **Questions** and **Polls** sheets and a **Sessions** sheet listing every session's Session ID. The **Session ID** column matches the session code (for example SESS-12), the Sessionboard ID or your Client Session ID. The mapping step names any required column a sheet is missing and waits until you choose one. Review lists every row that won't import, with its sheet, row number and reason, and **Download list** saves it. **Download**, next to **Import**, gives you the current import to correct and upload again.

where.path: Record Settings → Participant portal → Feedback → Import

entries.use_case: An organizer importing post-session survey results can download a pre-built template that already lists every session ID, map columns with clear guidance on what is required, and get a downloadable list of any rows that failed — so they can fix and re-import without losing the rows that did match.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer using the Participant Feedback beta asks how to import survey results from an external tool, or reports confusion about which columns are required during the import mapping step.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer on the Participant Feedback beta who collects session ratings outside Sessionboard and wants to display them in the speaker portal.
internal.staff_path: Record Settings → Participant portal → Feedback → Import
internal.gotchas: Feedback belongs to sessions, not people: rows match on Session ID or title, never a contact. Each import replaces the event's previous one. Download (export) answers 'nothing imported yet' when there is no import. When a Client Session ID looks like a code (another platform's SESS-21), the Client Session ID wins, and the template writes the Sessionboard ID for sessions whose code would collide.
internal.talk_track: The feedback import now works like every other import in Sessionboard: grab the template, map your columns with clear required-field labels, and get a report of any rows that didn't make it in so you can fix and retry.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should document the Import dialog steps — template download, required-column mapping, the rows-not-imported table and CSV export, and the post-import Download button on the Feedback settings page.
draft.why_use_it: Participant Feedback lets you surface session ratings and comments directly in the speaker portal so presenters can see how their sessions were received. You control which feedback is visible, when it appears, and who can see it. Importing feedback from an external survey tool keeps all post-event data in one place without manual data entry.

entries.title: See imported survey feedback on the session record and in reports
entries.summary: Imported survey feedback is no longer visible only to speakers. A **Survey feedback** tab on the session page and the session flyover shows the session's average rating and count, comments grouped by survey question, audience questions and poll results, with the import date and a link to the import settings. It does not depend on whether you have released feedback to speakers. The Report Builder gains six Session fields, **Imported Survey Rating (Avg)**, **Imported Survey Rating Count**, **Imported Survey Comment Count**, **Imported Audience Question Count**, **Imported Poll Count** and **Imported Survey Comments**, so you can compare sessions or export the feedback.

where.path: Program → session → Survey feedback; Reports → Report Builder → Sessions fields

entries.use_case: Event teams that import post-session survey data can now review ratings, comments and poll results for each session directly on the session record, without having to impersonate a speaker or leave the admin interface.

cs_action.note: Shows for every organization with Participant Feedback on (an Early Access Beta) once a survey file is imported. Anyone who can view the session sees it; a role limited to some sessions sees only those.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer asks how to review post-session survey results without previewing as a speaker, or when they have already set up a feedback import under Record Settings.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers who import participant survey data (e.g. from a post-event survey tool) and want their program team to see per-session ratings and comments in the admin.
internal.staff_path: Program → open a session → Survey feedback; Reports → Report Builder → search 'imported'
internal.gotchas: The tab is hidden entirely if the API returns null — no toast, no error. If a customer reports the tab is missing, confirm the org has the speaker_feedback preview on and that at least one feedback import row exists for the event.
internal.talk_track: Your team can now see exactly how attendees rated and commented on each session right on the session record — no need to switch views or impersonate a speaker.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should document the new Survey feedback tab on the admin session record, including what each section shows (ratings, comments by question, polls), the empty states, and the link to Feedback import settings.
draft.why_use_it: Participant Feedback brings post-event survey results — star ratings, open-ended comments, audience questions and poll tallies — into the session record so your team can evaluate session quality alongside the rest of the program data. Use it to identify top-rated sessions for future programming, spot recurring attendee concerns, and share structured feedback with speakers through the portal, all from one place.

entries.title: Partner-issued SSO portal links now work in the current portal
entries.summary: Sign-in links generated by Cvent, Google, Swoogo and similar partner platforms (the `/sso-link/…` format) now land speakers directly in their portal home instead of dropping them on an email/password login screen. When the link cannot be matched to a contact, the portal displays the reason clearly rather than showing a blank page.

where.path: Speaker portal sign-in (via partner-issued SSO link)

entries.use_case: Events that use Cvent, Swoogo or Google to issue portal access links no longer need to ask speakers to sign in a second time. Speakers click the partner link and land directly in their portal, with the correct account already selected.

cs_action.note: Fix is automatic for all events on the new UI (enabled since 2026-05-26). No setup required.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer reports that speakers arriving via Cvent exhibitor answer links, Swoogo or Google SSO links are landing on the password login screen instead of their portal.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any event using a partner platform (Cvent, Swoogo, Google) that generates /sso-link portal access URLs for speakers or exhibitors.
internal.gotchas: If the API returns an error (no contact for that email, or the person is an event admin), the portal now shows the API's reason text. Organizers should ensure contacts exist before partner links are distributed.
internal.talk_track: Partner-issued portal links now work end-to-end — speakers click the link from Cvent or Swoogo and land straight in their portal without a second login.

draft.docs_gap: Add a note explaining that partner-issued SSO portal links (Cvent exhibitor answers, Google, Swoogo) are supported and what error messages appear when a link cannot be matched to a contact.

entries.title: CfP form stays open when an admin session has expired
entries.summary: When a submitter returns to a call-for-proposals form after their admin sign-in has expired, the form now stays open and shows its own sign-in prompt instead of redirecting to the generic **Log in** page. SSO-only submitters who were previously stuck on the admin login screen are no longer affected.

where.path: Call for proposals submission form

entries.use_case: Returning submitters — especially those using SSO — no longer get stranded on the admin login page when their previous session has expired; they see the form's own sign-in and can continue without contacting support.

cs_action.note: Fix ships automatically; no configuration needed.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer reports that returning submitters or SSO users are being bounced to the admin login page instead of the form's sign-in.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any event using a CfP form with sub-sessions and SSO or returning submitters.
internal.gotchas: The companion API change (sessionboard-web-api#5328, making subsession-limit optional-auth) is independent and can ship separately; the UI fix alone resolves the redirect loop.
internal.talk_track: Submitters who come back to a form after their session expires now see the form's own sign-in instead of being sent to the admin login page — no more dead ends for SSO-only attendees.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should note that expired admin sessions are handled gracefully on forms with sub-sessions, keeping submitters on the form's own sign-in screen.

entries.title: Share Advocacy campaigns by link or embed, delete live campaigns, and see company card previews in Sessionboard Marketing
entries.summary: On the self-serve Marketing **Campaigns** page, a new **"I'll share a link or embed"** option lets organizers launch a Speakers, Sponsors, Exhibitors, or Attendees campaign without emailing anyone — the campaign hands out a shareable open link, an embeddable sign-up form, and a QR code via the new **Share it yourself** card. Live campaigns can now be **deleted** (with a confirmation step), and sponsor/exhibitor card previews correctly show **"Proud sponsor of"** / **"We're exhibiting at"** wording. The term **"animated card"** replaces "video card" throughout the campaign sheet and launch flow.

where.path: Marketing → Campaigns

entries.use_case: An organizer who wants speakers or attendees to share event content on their own sites or social channels — without sending any Sessionboard emails — can now launch a link-only campaign, copy the embed snippet, and drop it on a confirmation page or event website. They can also clean up finished campaigns by deleting them rather than leaving them paused.

cs_action.note: All changes are default-on for self-serve Marketing customers already on the Campaigns beta. No setup required.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks how to promote their event through speakers or attendees without sending emails from Sessionboard, or wants to embed a sign-up widget on their own site.
internal.who_should_get_it: Self-serve Sessionboard Marketing customers using the Campaigns (Advocacy) beta.
internal.staff_path: Marketing → Campaigns → New campaign or open a draft → Who → I'll share a link or embed
internal.gotchas: The 'I'll share a link or embed' option is not available on email-only campaign intents. Results for link-only campaigns show Shares / Clicks / Registrations — the 'Reached' tile is hidden because it would always be zero. Delete is permanent and irreversible; the confirmation dialog reminds users to pause instead if they want to keep results.
internal.talk_track: You can now launch an Advocacy campaign that never sends a single email — just grab the link or embed snippet and put it wherever your audience already is. And when a campaign has run its course, you can delete it to keep your list tidy.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should document the "I'll share a link or embed" who-option, the Share it yourself card (open link, QR code, embed snippet, Opens in / Open automatically controls, Preview dialog), the delete action on live campaigns, and the updated "animated card" terminology.
draft.why_use_it: Advocacy campaigns let you turn speakers, sponsors, exhibitors, and attendees into active promoters of your event. Each person gets a personalised card they can share on social media, embed on their site, or send to their own network — and you track every share, click, and registration it drives. Use it when you want word-of-mouth reach beyond your own email list, or when you need a ready-made embed for a registration confirmation page.

entries.title: Generating and recompiling prints works again in Europe
entries.summary: In the EU region, generating or recompiling a print from **Program > Print** failed with "Request failed" from November 8. A queue setting pointed at the wrong region after an infrastructure move. It was corrected on November 10, and print jobs that cannot be queued now fail with an error instead of waiting forever. US and Middle East events were not affected.

where.path: Program → Print → Generate or Recompile

entries.use_case: An EU organizer preparing a printed program before an event can generate and recompile it again; anyone who saw "Request failed" between November 8 and 10 just clicks Recompile.

cs_action.note: Tell EU customers who reported print failures (SB-11358, event 183) to click Recompile; nothing else is needed.

internal.when_to_bring_up: An EU customer reports a red "Request failed" when generating or recompiling a print.
internal.who_should_get_it: EU customers who use Print.
internal.staff_path: Program → Print → open a template → Recompile
internal.gotchas: Fixed live on 2026-11-10 by a configuration change (EU booklet queue URL); the code change in #5278 keeps a misconfigured queue from leaving jobs pending.
internal.talk_track: Printing works again in Europe; just recompile.

entries.title: One Campaigns list for your team and your event community
entries.summary: **Advocacy → Campaigns** now lists event community campaigns and team campaigns (Dispatch) together, with an **All / Your team / Event community** filter, search and status across both. **New campaign** asks **Who's sharing it?**, with **Your event community** as the default. The separate Dispatch row in the sidebar is gone; old Dispatch links open the list.

where.path: Marketing → Advocacy → Campaigns

entries.use_case: Everything that gets your event shared — by participants, exhibitors, attendees or your own staff — is now in one list, so you can see every campaign's shares and clicks side by side.

cs_action.note: Nothing to turn on. Team campaigns appear only for orgs with the Dispatch Early Access.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks where Dispatch went, or wants one view of everything being shared for an event.
internal.who_should_get_it: Every Advocacy customer; Dispatch beta orgs see team campaigns in the same list.
internal.staff_path: Event → Marketing → Advocacy → Campaigns; org → Marketing → Advocacy → Your team
internal.gotchas: Who's sharing it can't be changed after a campaign is created. The Dispatch sidebar row was removed; /marketing/dispatches redirects to the list.
internal.talk_track: Your team's posts and your event community's share cards are now in one Campaigns list, with a filter to switch between them.

entries.title: Delete Advocacy and team campaigns
entries.summary: Delete a campaign from its row menu, the campaign page or several at once from the list. An unshared draft asks a plain **Delete draft?**; a shared campaign lists what happens to posted links, results and sharers, asks you to type `DELETE`, and offers **Pause sharing instead** for an active campaign.

where.path: Marketing → Advocacy → Campaigns → ⋯ → Delete…

entries.use_case: Clear test and abandoned campaigns out of the list, with a clear warning before anything that has been shared disappears from your results.

cs_action.note: No setup. Restore is staff-only through support; do not offer it to customers.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer has test or duplicate campaigns cluttering the list.
internal.who_should_get_it: Every Advocacy customer.
internal.staff_path: Marketing → Advocacy → Campaigns → row ⋯ → Delete…; campaign → Campaign actions → Delete campaign
internal.gotchas: Deletes are soft; staff can restore from History → Deleted on request, but customer docs and copy deliberately promise no restore. Team campaign toasts keep an Undo.
internal.talk_track: You can delete a campaign from the list now. Shared ones ask you to type DELETE first, and you can pause instead if you want to keep the results.

entries.title: Team campaigns send on schedule, pause and resume, and reach Microsoft Teams
entries.summary: Team campaigns (Dispatch) now send each post on its date by themselves — dated posts, **T-N** posts at 9:00 event time and **Day N** posts — and can be paused and resumed. Teammates get their posts in Slack, **Microsoft Teams** or email, team campaigns count in the event's Advocacy **Analytics** and **Activity**, and **Send now** asks you to finish a post whose asset isn't ready.

where.path: Marketing → Advocacy → Campaigns → Your team

entries.use_case: Set up a month of team posts once and let them go out on schedule, pause them when timing is wrong, and see your staff's shares next to your community's.

cs_action.note: Dispatch is an Early Access beta; enable it for the org.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer wants staff to share event content on a schedule, or uses Microsoft Teams rather than Slack.
internal.who_should_get_it: Dispatch beta orgs, especially sales-led and membership teams.
internal.staff_path: Org → Early Access → Dispatch; event → Marketing → Advocacy → New campaign → Your team
internal.gotchas: Posts more than 24 h late are not auto-sent; use Send now. Teams delivery needs the Sessionboard app added in the customer's Teams tenant.
internal.talk_track: Your team's posts now go out on their own on the dates you set, you can pause them anytime, and they land in Slack, Teams or email.

entries.title: Launch a campaign with one link or an embed, no invites
entries.summary: On Quick Launch's Recipients step, **I'll share a link or embed** runs a Participants, Groups or Attendees campaign with nobody invited: copy the campaign link or its QR code, or put the embed on your site. The Share console previews a sample person from your event, and after **Activate campaign** you land on the campaign page with **Campaign launched.** and the next step. Groups link-only campaigns accept every exhibitor and sponsor on the event; participant embeds admit every participant.

where.path: Marketing → Advocacy → Campaigns → New campaign → Recipients

entries.use_case: Get a campaign out in minutes without building a list or sending a single email — drop the link in a newsletter or the embed on your website.

cs_action.note: No setup.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer has no clean list of attendees, exhibitors or speakers yet, or wants to share through their own channels.
internal.who_should_get_it: Every Advocacy customer.
internal.staff_path: Marketing → Advocacy → Campaigns → New campaign → Your event community → Recipients → I'll share a link or embed
internal.gotchas: The campaign page still shows 'No recipients assigned yet' on link-only campaigns; that is expected.
internal.talk_track: You can now launch a campaign without inviting anyone: share one link or embed it, and anyone who opens it makes their own card.

entries.title: Exhibitor and sponsor cards, per-company links and new companies on the open link
entries.summary: Groups campaigns get **Badge**, **Banner** and **Photo** card styles in exhibiting and sponsoring versions; the role line follows each company's type, with booth or tier, and the company name prints once. **CTA link source → Group field — per company** points each company's shares at its own page. **Let companies that aren't on the event yet sign up** adds a company typed on the open link to the event as an exhibitor or sponsor.

where.path: Marketing → Advocacy → Campaigns → Groups campaign

entries.use_case: Exhibitors share a card that says exactly what they are doing at the show, link to their own booth page, and booth staff from companies not yet in Sessionboard can still join.

cs_action.note: New-company sign-up is on for new campaigns and off for existing ones.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer runs exhibitor or sponsor advocacy, or their exhibitor list in Sessionboard is incomplete.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers with exhibitors or sponsors on their events.
internal.staff_path: Marketing → Advocacy → Campaigns → Groups campaign → Recipients / Share tab → Let companies that aren't on the event yet sign up
internal.gotchas: New companies are created with method 'Advocacy open link'; same-name org accounts are reused; 25/hour/org cap.
internal.talk_track: Exhibitor and sponsor cards now say 'Visit us at Booth 1214' or 'Gold Sponsor', can link to each company's own page, and new companies can join through the open link.

entries.title: Advocacy embeds for participants, exhibitors and sponsors
entries.summary: Besides attendees, you can now embed a participant's card (`advocacy-speaking`) and a company's card or signup form (`advocacy-exhibiting`) on your own pages. Every embed shows the card image and one **Make it yours** button, opens in a new window or a popover (`open-in`, `auto-open`), becomes a bottom sheet on phones, respects reduced motion, and keeps its submit button unavailable until consent is ticked. **Preview** runs each embed before you paste it.

where.path: Marketing → Advocacy → Campaigns → campaign → Share tab → Embed on your page

entries.use_case: Ask people to share at the moment they're already on your page — the speaker portal, exhibitor manual or confirmation page — with their own card ready to personalize.

cs_action.note: Embeds need the manual embeds prod publish.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer has a speaker portal, exhibitor manual or registration confirmation page that accepts HTML.
internal.who_should_get_it: Every Advocacy customer with a website or portal they control.
internal.staff_path: Marketing → Advocacy → Campaigns → campaign → Share
internal.gotchas: Embeds prod publish is manual. The attendee embed no longer shows direct share buttons (Make it yours only). Speaker and company cards email the editing link, so open-in has no effect on them.
internal.talk_track: You can now put a participant's or exhibitor's own share card on any page you control, and it can open right there in a popover.

entries.title: Make it yours: name prefix and credentials, photo framing, three post tones, card sizes and LinkedIn review
entries.summary: On their share page, advocates can add a **Name prefix** and **Credentials after your name** ("Dr. Maya Chen, MD"), frame their photo, pick a post written in three tones (**Excited**, **Professional**, **Short**), download the card as **Square**, **Link preview** or **Stories**, and post to LinkedIn with their card as an image after reviewing the post.

where.path: Advocate share page

entries.use_case: Advocates post a card that looks like theirs, with credentials and a well-framed photo, in words that sound like them — so more of them actually post.

cs_action.note: No setup. Admin-written share variants override the three drafts.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer's speakers complain the card isn't right or don't post.
internal.who_should_get_it: Every Advocacy customer, especially medical and scientific events where credentials matter.
internal.staff_path: Campaign → Preview as… to see the share page
internal.gotchas: The admin's own share variants win; drafts are generated only when the campaign has none.
internal.talk_track: Your speakers can now add their credentials, frame their photo, pick a tone for their post and download the card in the right size for each network.

entries.title: Rewards, contests and results by channel
entries.summary: Add a **Milestone** (bring 3 people, get VIP lounge access) or a **Contest** (top 10 by registrations) to any campaign, with an unlock email and an optional first-name leaderboard. Advocates see **Your results** on their share page, plus **Share…** on phones and **Email a colleague**. Campaign Analytics adds **Results by channel** and a full **Top advocates** table; bots, self-referrals and duplicate people never count.

where.path: Marketing → Advocacy → Campaigns → campaign → Rewards; Analytics

entries.use_case: Give advocates a reason to share more than once and see exactly which channel and which person brought registrations.

cs_action.note: No setup.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer wants to run a referral contest or prove which channel worked.
internal.who_should_get_it: Every Advocacy customer.
internal.staff_path: Marketing → Advocacy → Campaigns → campaign → Rewards → Add reward
internal.gotchas: Registrations count from Sessionboard registration or a page with the website tag recording a conversion named Registration.
internal.talk_track: You can now reward your best advocates with milestones or contests, and see results by channel.

entries.title: Participants (custom roles included) and the Animated format
entries.summary: The Speakers audience is now **Participants** and includes every participant role on the event, custom roles such as Panelists included. The video card format is now **Animated · Moving graphic**, and session cards print each person's role under their name.

where.path: Marketing → Advocacy → Campaigns → New campaign → Build

entries.use_case: Panelists, coordinators and any custom role get a card automatically, and the format name says what it is.

cs_action.note: No setup. Card and post copy ('I'm speaking') is unchanged.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer uses custom session roles.
internal.who_should_get_it: Every Advocacy customer.
internal.staff_path: Marketing → Advocacy → Campaigns → New campaign → Build → Who's sharing / Format
internal.gotchas: Public embed names (advocacy-speaking, speaker-id) are unchanged.
internal.talk_track: Every participant role on your sessions, including custom ones, now gets a card, and the animated card is labelled Animated.

entries.title: Arabic, right to left, across Advocacy
entries.summary: Set an event's language to Arabic and its share pages, share cards, suggested posts, open-link signup page, embeds and Advocacy emails read in Arabic, right to left, with an Arabic font on the card. Embeds also take `language="ar"`.

where.path: Advocate share page, embeds and emails

entries.use_case: Middle East events can run Advocacy in Arabic end to end.

cs_action.note: Arabic strings need a native-speaker review before customers rely on them.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer runs an Arabic-language event.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers with events in the Middle East.
internal.staff_path: Event → Settings → Event details → Language
internal.gotchas: Absolutely positioned card layouts (split, date pill) are not mirrored; text inside is correct. The registration confirmation {{advocacy_share_card}} block is English-only.
internal.talk_track: Advocacy now works in Arabic, right to left, from the share page to the emails.

entries.title: Track conversions from Advocacy with one website tag
entries.summary: See who lands, clicks your CTA and registers or buys after clicking an advocate's link. Sessionboard pages need nothing; on your own site, add the one Sessionboard website tag, set CTAs, conversion pages and the attribution window, and run **Check installation**. **Send setup instructions to someone technical** also works for custom domains and email sending domains. Campaign Analytics adds **Conversions**.

where.path: Marketing → Advocacy → Campaigns → campaign → Conversion tracking

entries.use_case: Prove what advocacy is worth in registrations and revenue, not just clicks.

cs_action.note: No setup for Sessionboard pages; the customer's web team adds the tag for their own site.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks what advocacy actually drove, or registers on another platform.
internal.who_should_get_it: Every Advocacy customer, especially those registering on Cvent, Swoogo or their own site.
internal.staff_path: Marketing → Advocacy → Campaigns → campaign → Conversion tracking
internal.gotchas: The old /amplify-conversions pixel and sb_ref are retired; links now carry sb_click.
internal.talk_track: Add one tag to your site and Advocacy shows you who registered or bought after clicking each advocate's link.

entries.title: Share your own videos, clips, audiograms and quote cards through Advocacy
entries.summary: A fourth format, **Media**, lets advocates share items from your Media library — videos, clips, audiograms, slide videos and quote cards, up to 50 per campaign — each with their own tracked link. Pick from the library or upload an MP4 or MOV (up to 500 MB and 3 minutes), or start from **Media**, **Clips** or **Quotes** with **Share with advocates**. Advocates post videos natively to LinkedIn, on the channels the campaign allows.

where.path: Marketing → Advocacy → Campaigns → New campaign → Media format; or Media library → item → Share with advocates

entries.use_case: An event team has produced speaker clips, audiograms and quote cards and wants advocates to share them on LinkedIn with tracked links — not just the auto-generated share cards. The Media campaign format lets them pick up to 50 existing media items and send advocates a personalised link that posts the video or image natively to LinkedIn.

cs_action.note: Available to any customer with Advocacy. No extra enablement step required.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer has produced clips or audiograms and wants advocates to share them on LinkedIn with tracked links, or when they ask whether Advocacy supports video sharing.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers actively using Advocacy who also produce post-event content (clips, audiograms, slide videos, quote cards) in the Media library.
internal.staff_path: Marketing → Advocacy → Campaigns → New campaign → choose Media as the format
internal.gotchas: A Media campaign cannot be activated with zero items attached (returns a 422). Max 50 items per campaign. Only items that are fully exported, not archived, and have a Sessionboard-hosted file are eligible. MP4 files ≤ 200 MB and ≤ 10 minutes post natively as LinkedIn videos; larger or longer files fall back to text + tracked link. Native LinkedIn posting respects the campaign's share channels (web-api #5334).
internal.talk_track: You've already made the clips and audiograms — now you can put them directly in advocates' hands with a single tracked link per person, and see exactly who shared which video.

draft.docs_gap: The Advocacy guide should add a section documenting the Media campaign format: how to create one, how to attach items from the Media library (including the "Share with advocates" shortcut), the 50-item cap, eligibility rules for media items, how native LinkedIn video posting works, and how share reporting differs from card campaigns.
draft.why_use_it: Advocacy lets you turn speakers, sponsors and attendees into a distributed promotion channel by giving each person a personalised, tracked link to share on social media. With the Media format, you choose exactly which videos, clips, audiograms, slide videos or quote cards each campaign promotes, so advocates share polished, on-brand content rather than a generic card. Every share is recorded against the advocate's link, so you can see who shared what and measure reach across the whole campaign.

entries.title: Advocacy emails come from a person, with your branding and one-click unsubscribe
entries.summary: Every Advocacy and team campaign email now comes from "*Person* via Sessionboard" with Reply-To that person, carries your brand kit, has one button with a plain fallback link, and ends with why the person got it, **Why am I getting this?** and **Unsubscribe**. Subjects are calm and specific, such as "Your share card for *your event* is ready". Unsubscribe covers the campaign or all Advocacy email from your organization.

where.path: Emails sent by Notify, reminders, team campaigns, rewards and Email a colleague

entries.use_case: Advocates trust an email from a colleague they can reply to far more than one from a no-reply address, so more of them open it and share.

cs_action.note: No setup. The default Notify subject changed; subjects customers typed are kept.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer says advocates ignore or distrust the share emails, or asks about unsubscribe and compliance.
internal.who_should_get_it: Every Advocacy and Dispatch customer.
internal.staff_path: Campaign → Campaign actions → Notify recipients (preview); any team campaign → Send test
internal.gotchas: Unsubscribed people are skipped by Notify, reminders, team campaign sends and nudges, and reward emails. Opt-outs are stored as an address hash. One-off emails people ask for carry no unsubscribe link.
internal.talk_track: Share emails now come from you, by name, with your branding, and anyone can reply to you or unsubscribe in one click.
